subject.title: [Bug]: iOS app fails to connect over Tailscale CGNAT (100.x.x.x) — wss:// required but WebSocket upgrade silently dropped

question: Which Tailscale transport should iOS officially support for first-use remote Gateway pairing: secure Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS only, direct CGNAT plaintext by explicit opt-in, or public/split-host wss as the primary advanced path?
rationale: The current source intentionally blocks plaintext 100.x and .ts.net setup while the user report shows the secure path failing; changing that behavior would alter the mobile Gateway trust boundary and cannot be chosen safely by automation.

options.title: Keep Secure-Only Tailscale UX
options.body: Require Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS or another wss endpoint, improve iOS diagnostics and setup guidance when the endpoint is unreachable or not TLS-capable, and leave raw 100.x blocked.

options.title: Approve Direct Tailnet Exception
options.body: Allow a narrow user-confirmed or settings-gated ws:// path for Tailscale CGNAT addresses with clear warnings, tests, and no public-host downgrade.

options.title: Route Through Public wss Guidance
options.body: Treat direct CGNAT as unsupported for iOS and document the advanced public or split-host wss recipe tracked by related remote-pairing issues.

recommendation.title: Keep Secure-Only Tailscale UX
recommendation.body: Require Tailscale Serve/MagicDNS or another wss endpoint, improve iOS diagnostics and setup guidance when the endpoint is unreachable or not TLS-capable, and leave raw 100.x blocked.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on TLS trust hardening and mobile setup route selection, including the overlapping merged route-list fix.
